vsm2.20:76.1: The headings of what was called above “the immaterial septad” are these:
vsm2.20:76.2:
(1) by groups, (2) by pairs, (3) by moments, (4) by series, (5) by removal of false view,
(6) by abolition of conceit, (7) by ending of attachment.
vsm2.20:77.1: 1. Herein, by groups means the states belonging to the contact pentad.
vsm2.20:77.2: How? Here, “he comprehends by groups” means that a bhikkhu considers thus:
vsm2.20:77.3:
The states belonging to the contact pentad arising in the comprehending of head hairs as “impermanent,
painful, not-self”; the states belonging to the contact pentad arising in the comprehending of body
hairs as … in the contemplation of brain as “impermanent, painful, not-self”
vsm2.20:77.4:
—all these states disintegrate section by section, term by term, like crackling sesame seeds put into a hot pan,
each without reaching the next: therefore they are impermanent, painful, not-self.
vsm2.20:77.5: This, firstly, is the method according to the Discourse on Purification.
vsm2.20:78.1:
According to the Discourse on the Noble Ones’ Heritages, however, he is said to “comprehend by groups” when by means of a subsequent
consciousness he comprehends as “impermanent, painful, not-self” that consciousness which occurred comprehending
materiality as “impermanent, painful, not-self” in the seven instances of the material septad given above.
vsm2.20:78.2: As this method is more suitable we shall therefore confine ourselves to it in explaining the rest.
vsm2.20:79.1:
2. By pairs: after the bhikkhu has comprehended as “impermanent, painful, not-self” the materiality of the “taking
up and putting down” (§46f.), he comprehends that consciousness with which he was comprehending
the materiality too as “impermanent, painful, not-self” by means of a subsequent consciousness.
vsm2.20:79.2:
After he has comprehended as “impermanent, painful, not-self” the materiality of the “disappearance of what grows old in each
stage” and that “arising from nutriment,” “arising from temperature,” “kamma-born,” “consciousness-originated” and “natural,”
he comprehends that consciousness too as “impermanent, painful, not-self” by means of a subsequent consciousness.
vsm2.20:79.3: In this way he is said to comprehend by pairs.
vsm2.20:80.1:
3. By moments: after the bhikkhu has comprehended as “impermanent, painful, not-self” the materiality of the “taking
up and putting down,” he comprehends that first consciousness with which he was comprehending the materiality as “impermanent,
painful, not-self” by means of a second consciousness, and that second consciousness by means of a third, and the third
by means of a fourth, and the fourth by means of a fifth, and that too he comprehends as “impermanent, painful, not-self.”
vsm2.20:80.2:
After he has comprehended as “impermanent, painful, not-self” the materiality of “disappearance of what
grows old in each stage” and that “arising from nutriment,” “arising from temperature,” “kamma-born,”
“consciousness-originated” and “natural,” he comprehends that first consciousness as “impermanent, painful,
not-self” by means of a second consciousness, and that second consciousness by means of a third, and the third by means
of a fourth, and the fourth by means of a fifth, and that too he comprehends as “impermanent, painful, not-self.”
vsm2.20:80.3: Comprehending thus four consciousnesses from each discerning of materiality he is said to comprehend by moments.
vsm2.20:81.1:
4. By series: after he has comprehended as “impermanent, painful, not-self” the materiality of the “taking
up and putting down,” he comprehends that first consciousness as “impermanent, painful,
not-self” by means of a second consciousness, and the second by means of a third, and the third by means of a fourth
… and the tenth by means of an eleventh, and that too he comprehends as “impermanent, painful, not-self.”
vsm2.20:81.2:
After he has comprehended as “impermanent, painful, not-self” the materiality of the “disappearance of what grows old in each
stage” and that “arising from nutriment,” “arising from temperature,” “kamma-born,” “consciousness-originated” and “natural,”
he comprehends that consciousness as “impermanent, painful, not-self” by means of a second consciousness, and the second by means
of a third, … and the tenth by means of an eleventh, and that too he comprehends as “impermanent, painful, not-self.”
vsm2.20:81.3: It would be possible to go on comprehending it in this way with serial insight even for a whole day.
vsm2.20:81.4:
But both the material meditation subject and the immaterial meditation subject become familiar
when the comprehending is taken as far as the tenth consciousness.
vsm2.20:81.5: That is why it is said that it can be stopped at the tenth.
vsm2.20:81.6: It is when he comprehends in this way that he is said to comprehend by series.
vsm2.20:82.1:
5. By removal of false view, 6. by abolition of conceit, 7. by ending of attachment:
there is no individual method for any of these three.
vsm2.20:82.2:
But when he has discerned this materiality as described above and this immateriality as described here,
then he sees that there is no living being over and above the material and the immaterial.
vsm2.20:82.3: As soon as he no longer sees a being, the perception of a being is removed.
vsm2.20:82.4:
When he discerns formations with consciousness from which perception of a being has been removed,
then false view does not arise in him.
vsm2.20:82.5: When false view does not arise in him, then false view is said to be removed.
vsm2.20:82.6: When he discerns formations with consciousness from which false view has been removed, then conceit does not arise in him.
vsm2.20:82.7: When conceit does not arise, conceit is said to be abolished.
vsm2.20:82.8: When he discerns formations with consciousness from which conceit has been abolished, then craving does not arise in him.
vsm2.20:82.9: When craving does not arise in him, attachment is said to be ended. This firstly is what is said in the Discourse on Purification.
vsm2.20:83.1:
But in the Discourse on the Noble Ones’ Heritages, after setting forth the headings thus: “As removal of false view,
as abolition of conceit, as ending of attachment,” the following method is set forth:
vsm2.20:83.2: “There is no removal of false view in one who takes it thus, ‘I see with insight, my insight’;
vsm2.20:83.3:
there is removal of false view in one who takes it thus, ‘Only formations see
formations with insight, comprehend, define, discern, and delimit them.’
vsm2.20:83.4: There is no abolition of conceit in one who takes it thus, ‘I see thoroughly with insight, I see well with insight’;
vsm2.20:83.5:
there is abolition of conceit in one who takes it thus, ‘Only formations see formations with insight,
comprehend, define, discern, and delimit them.’
vsm2.20:83.6: There is no ending of attachment in one who is pleased with insight thus, ‘I am able to see with insight’;
vsm2.20:83.7:
there is ending of attachment in one who takes it thus, ‘Only formations see formations with insight,
comprehend, define, discern, and delimit them.’
vsm2.20:84.1:
“There is removal of false view in one who sees thus: ‘If formations were self, it would
be right to take them as self; but being not-self they are taken as self.
vsm2.20:84.2:
Therefore they are not-self in the sense of no power being exercisable over them; they are impermanent in the sense of non-existence
after having come to be; they are painful in the sense of oppression by rise and fall.’
vsm2.20:85.1:
“There is abolition of conceit in one who sees thus: ‘If formations were permanent, it would
be right to take them as permanent; but being impermanent they are taken as permanent.
vsm2.20:85.2:
Therefore they are impermanent in the sense of non-existence after having come to be; they are painful in the sense
of oppression by rise and fall; they are not-self in the sense of no power being exercisable over them.’
vsm2.20:86.1:
“There is ending of attachment in one who sees thus: ‘If formations were pleasant, it would
be right to take them as pleasant; but being painful they are taken as pleasant.
vsm2.20:86.2:
Therefore they are painful in the sense of oppression by rise and fall; they are impermanent in the sense of non-existence
after having come to be; they are not-self in the sense of no power being exercisable over them.’
vsm2.20:86.3: “Thus there comes to be the removal of false view in one who sees formations as not-self;
vsm2.20:86.4: there comes to be the abolishing of conceit in one who sees them as impermanent;
vsm2.20:86.5: there comes to be the ending of attachment in one who sees them as painful.
vsm2.20:86.6: So this insight is valid in each instance.”
vsm2.20:88.1: This is how he comprehends formations by attributing the three characteristics to them by means of the immaterial septad.
vsm2.20:88.2: At this stage both the material meditation subject and the immaterial meditation subject have become familiar to him.
vsm2.20:89.1:
The Eighteen Principal Insights

Having thus become familiar with the material and immaterial meditation subjects,
vsm2.20:89.2:
and so having penetrated here already a part of those eighteen principal insights which are later on to be attained in all
their aspects by means of full-understanding as abandoning starting with contemplation of dissolution,
vsm2.20:89.3: he consequently abandons things opposed to what he has already penetrated.
vsm2.20:90.1:
Eighteen principal insights is a term for understanding that consists in the kinds of insight
beginning with contemplation of impermanence.
vsm2.20:90.2: Now, as regards these: (1) one who develops the contemplation of impermanence abandons the perception of permanence,
vsm2.20:90.3: (2) one who develops the contemplation of pain abandons the perception of pleasure,
vsm2.20:90.4: (3) one who develops the contemplation of not-self abandons the perception of self,
vsm2.20:90.5: (4) one who develops the contemplation of dispassion abandons delighting,
vsm2.20:90.6: (5) one who develops the contemplation of fading away abandons greed,
vsm2.20:90.7: (6) one who develops the contemplation of cessation abandons origination,
vsm2.20:90.8: (7) one who develops the contemplation of relinquishment abandons grasping,
vsm2.20:90.9: (8) one who develops the contemplation of destruction abandons the perception of compactness,
vsm2.20:90.10: (9) one who develops the contemplation of fall of formations abandons accumulation of kamma,
vsm2.20:90.11: (10) one who develops the contemplation of change abandons the perception of lastingness,
vsm2.20:90.12: (11) one who develops the contemplation of the signless abandons the sign,
vsm2.20:90.13: (12) one who develops the contemplation of the desireless abandons desire,
vsm2.20:90.14: (13) one who develops the contemplation of voidness abandons misinterpreting (insistence),
vsm2.20:90.15:
(14) one who develops the insight into states that is higher understanding abandons
misinterpreting (insistence) due to grasping at a core,
vsm2.20:90.16: (15) one who develops correct knowledge and vision abandons misinterpreting (insistence) due to confusion,
vsm2.20:90.17: (16) one who develops the contemplation of danger abandons misinterpreting (insistence) due to reliance,
vsm2.20:90.18: (17) one who develops the contemplation of reflection abandons non-reflection,
vsm2.20:90.19: (18) one who develops the contemplation of turning away abandons misinterpreting (insistence) due to bondage (see Paṭis I 32f.).
vsm2.20:91.1: Now the meditator has seen formations by means of the three characteristics beginning with impermanence,
vsm2.20:91.2: and so he has therefore already penetrated among these eighteen insights the contemplations of impermanence, pain, and not-self.
vsm2.20:91.3:
And then (1) the contemplation of impermanence and (11) the contemplation of the signless
are one in meaning and different only in the letter,
vsm2.20:91.4: and so are (2) the contemplation of pain and (12) the contemplation of the desireless,
vsm2.20:91.5: and so are (3) the contemplation of not-self and (13) the contemplation of voidness (see Paṭis II 63).
vsm2.20:91.6: Consequently these have been penetrated by him as well.
vsm2.20:91.7: But (14) insight into states that is higher understanding is all kinds of insight,
vsm2.20:91.8: and (15) correct knowledge and vision is included in purification by overcoming doubt (Ch. XIX).
vsm2.20:91.9: Consequently, these two have been penetrated by him as well.
vsm2.20:91.10: As to the remaining kinds of insight, some have been penetrated and some not. We shall deal with them below.
vsm2.20:92.1: For it was with reference only to what has already been penetrated that it was said above:
vsm2.20:92.2:
“having thus become familiar with the material and immaterial meditation subjects, and so having penetrated
here already a part of those eighteen principal insights, which are later on to be attained in all
their aspects by means of full understanding as abandoning starting with contemplation of dissolution,
vsm2.20:92.3: he consequently abandons things opposed to what he has already penetrated” (§89).
